correctness.rationale: By symmetric PBH, leaving two nonbridge twins uncontrolled makes their difference an invisible eigenvector, giving both quotas. For an exact-quota baseline the selected vertex equations imply that omitted nonbridge entries u,v have opposite entries at the respective gateways. The omitted-vertex equations are (ap-lambda)u=0 and (bq-lambda)v=0; a gateway equation is (lambda-ap)u+c(v-u)=0. With c>0 a nonzero solution has u=v nonzero and ap=bq. At resonance this is the unique invisible direction and has no zero in the four omitted coordinates, so any extra actuator removes it. This proves the all-set criterion and independence of positive c. The resonant minimum-set count has 2(p-1)(q-1) sets containing one gateway and (p-1)+(q-1) sets containing neither, not four times the baseline count; the claimed coefficient and polynomial are correct. For zero forcing two initial nonbridge whites are an obstruction until one of them is forced, which cannot first happen while both are white. A baseline stalls. From an admissible superset, if a gateway is initially blue, use a blue nonbridge neighbor on that side to force the sole possible remaining nonbridge white; if all nonbridge vertices on a side are blue, they can force the gateway. A fully blue side then forces across the bridge if needed, and the other side finishes. This spells out the force in the frozen wording without requiring a gateway to force while it still has two white neighbors. The finite modular checks were inspected, not rerun; the real-field proof does not rely on them.
